purpose: Sketch of a series of translators, the strip of the share of function words (decisions 2 and 3 of .steering/20261028-third-input-and-style, design in style-design.md there): for each translation a row of relief tiles of version 1 (mean V and A of a run) at N equal runs, and under it a strip of N cells whose grey is the share of the run's tokens in a fixed external list of function words. The strip is a layer outside the rule (emotion to form), added by the makers; it is called the share of function words, not style. A block permutation of the translation labels gives a reference for whether the mean shares differ more than label noise. Images only.
fixed_before_running: Written on 2026-10-28 and committed before the script was run. Choices made after seeing values: the quantity (the share of function words, with the groups as a supplement) was chosen after version 3 (results 0d9744b) was seen, in particular after the main session saw that the words of V = A = 0 selected for the first translation include more prepositions and connectives (of, that, as, from, then) than the other two; fixing the list by its SHA-256 does not make this a preregistration. The main unit of 12 runs (instead of 60) was chosen on 2026-10-28 from a rough estimate made from the counts of version 3 (differences between translations of about 1 to 2 points, against a binomial spread of about 4 points at 150 tokens and about 2 points at 750 tokens), an estimate not checked by computation (decision 3 there); the fixed width of the scale was set knowing that estimate. The list: the tabulated words of Binongo 2003 (the source of the list of [W48]) could not be obtained (the paper is closed; external/function-words-20261028/FETCH.md), so the English stopwords of NLTK were taken, the other candidate named in the design. The groups were derived by works/function_word_groups.py from the Brown corpus and the universal tag map of NLTK, without reading the translations. Not seen before: any share of these texts, any relief tile at 12 or 30 runs, any value of the permutation. The reading uses blocks of one run of 12 (about 750 tokens), chosen after the results of version 3 under blocks of six runs of 60 (its 95th percentiles and the sensitivity to blocks of 12 runs) had been seen. Changed after the review before running (no high finding): the frame drawn outside the strip, the font and all tiles checked before any figure is written, the relief points of every N recorded, one reading enforced, the script of the groups pinned by its SHA-256, the groups and the hyphenated words described.
base_conditions: works/conditions/sketch_translations.json (texts, extraction, tokenize, the cut into runs at k T // N by works/sketch_translations.runs, lexicon, generator, relief: all taken from it unchanged; only N differs)

function_words.name: NLTK English stopwords
function_words.source: nltk/nltk_data, packages/corpora/stopwords.zip, member stopwords/english, at commit 550b6625bcef1f2abff2ff770a5a0d272c9c6b2a (the zip was last changed in 98e14261eaec2244af1db4ec5b282112444495aa); external/function-words-20261028/FETCH.md
function_words.use: taken as published, no word added or removed. The list holds pieces of contractions (don, t, ll, ve, ...) that the tokenizer of the generator never yields (it keeps don't as one token), and it holds the whole contractions (don't, it's, ...), which it does yield; it also holds some adverbs and verbs (very, just, own, be, have, do)

share: per run: (tokens of the run that are words of the list) / (tokens of the run), tokens of atact.lexicon.tokenize; per group the same with the words of the group only, so the groups add up to the share (up to rounding)
groups_source: works/function_word_groups.py: for each word of the list, the universal tag (Petrov, Das and McDonald 2012, NLTK taggers/universal_tagset.zip en-brown.map) that the word most often has in the tagged Brown corpus of NLTK (corpora/brown.zip), matched in lower case; ADP, CONJ, DET and PRON are kept as groups, every other tag and a word absent from Brown are 'other'. By that map, for example, subordinating conjunctions (if, because, while, until, than, that) fall in ADP, possessive her in DET, to in PRT (other), and contracted pronoun-verb forms (he's, i'm, it's) in PRT (other); all (PRT), there (PRT), don't (VERB), own (ADJ), so, then and once (ADV) also fall in other; this is left as the map gives it. The tag of each word, the share of its most frequent tag and its count in Brown are printed by the script

scale.fixed: the grey of a cell runs linearly from white at (pooled share - fixed_width / 2) to black at (pooled share + fixed_width / 2), clipped, the pooled share being the function tokens of the three translations over their tokens (the same for every N); the width is about 2.7 binomial standard deviations of a share near 0.5 at 750 tokens on each side; cells clipped are counted
scale.percentile: supplement: white at the 5th and black at the 95th percentile (numpy.percentile, linear) of the shares of all cells of the three translations at that N, clipped
scale.legend: for each N and scale a separate bar with the share written at both ends and the middle; the statistics are computed on the shares, never on the greys

statistic: for the shares x_t,k of the three translations t at the runs k: m_t = mean over k of x_t,k; S = max over t of |m_t - mean of the three m|; the same for each group (the group's share)

permutation.rng: numpy.random.default_rng(seed + j) for entry j of blocks; for each permutation and each block, rng.permutation(3); the share and every group use the same seed, so the same relabellings
permutation.scheme: the runs are cut into consecutive blocks of block_runs runs; in each block the three labels are permuted, one permutation for every run of the block, independently between blocks; slot t takes, block by block, the runs of the translation that the permutation puts in slot t; S is recomputed on the slots. Null: inside a block the labels are exchangeable

blocks.note: a block of about 750 tokens, near the six runs of about 900 tokens of version 3; 6^12 distinct relabellings

permutation.reported: for every entry and for the share and each group: the observed S, the departures m_t - mean, the mean shares, the 95th percentile of S (numpy.percentile, linear) and the share of permutations with S at or above the observed

reading: written before running, for the share at 12 runs with blocks of one run only: if the observed S exceeds the 95th percentile of S under the permutation, the mean shares are reported as 'distinguishable from the relabelling of blocks', otherwise as 'insufficient evidence under this null' (not 'no difference'). The groups and the other block sizes are reported only, without a reading and without correction for their number. The strip is drawn in both cases; no test is made of single cells or of where the strips cross.

figure.tiles: per translation one row of N relief tiles of version 1 (works/sketch_translations.run_point and relief.tile with eps, relief.grey under the common scale, origin lower left) on a field of tile_px = (row_width_px - (N - 1) tile_gap_px) // N (192 px at 12 runs, 72 at 30, 32 at 60; version 1 drew about 106 px, so a tile can look finer or coarser than in version 1); the rows in the order of the translations of the base conditions, top to bottom; no labels in the images
figure.strip: under each row, after strip_gap_px, a strip of N cells as wide as the tiles above them and strip_height_ratio of their height; darker is a larger share; framed: the black line of frame_px lies outside the cells (above in the gap, below, and in a white margin of frame_px left and right that every variant has, so each image is row_width_px + 2 frame_px wide)
figure.variants: strip (the strip after a white margin), framed (the same with a black frame of frame_px around the strip), none (the tiles alone, to judge whether the strip changes how the tiles are read); for the fixed scale all three, for the percentile scale strip and framed

outputs: results/sketch_translations_style/sketch_translations_style.json and results/sketch_translations_style/runs{N}_{fixed,percentile}_{strip,framed}.png, runs{N}_none.png and runs{N}_{fixed,percentile}_legend.png for N = 12, 30, 60
reported: the shares per run (tokens, function tokens, share, groups), the scales (pooled share, the ends of both scales, cells clipped), the tests, the size of the list and of each group, and the relief point (V, A, Z, unmatched) of every run at every N
not_claimed: Not a signature of a translator and not a measure of style: one story per translator, so the share mixes the translator's choices, the edition and the phrasing of this one text, the share of dialogue, and the place of the scene (runs at the same index stand only approximately at the same place). The tokenizer keeps hyphenated words as one token (a form such as to-day or no-one is not a word of the list), so a translation that hyphenates more has a lower share for that reason alone. The renderings of names (the largest difference of version 3) do not enter this quantity at all. A shift in one function word can be offset by another, so a share near the others does not mean the same function words. The runs are not independent samples; the binomial spread is a rough guide only, and the test is about the mean share of the whole text, not about the cells. The block permutation keeps the dependence inside a block and breaks it across blocks. The list, its groups, the unit, the scale and the grey are the makers' choices; the groups are those of one tag map and one corpus.
